question: Why did the integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still show a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits?
expect: premise false: after system expansion the net climate-change impact was negative, −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t (a net benefit) (abstract)
rendered:
<document title="Environmental and Preliminary Economic Assessment of Integrated Resource Recovery from Spent Fluid Catalytic Cracking Catalysts">

=== page 1 ===
- Before product-substitution credits, the climate-change impacts of the wet-recovery and leaching-residue-valorization stages were 1,536.56 and 1,940.11 kg CO2-eq, respectively.

=== page 8 ===
- After system expansion, all 16 main EF 3.1 impact categories exhibited net negative results, indicating net environmental benefits under the adopted product-substitution assumptions.
- The net climate-change impact was −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t of spent FCC catalyst.
- However, the foreground operating cost was still 5,763.35 Chinese yuan (CNY) per t of spent catalyst.

The integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still showed a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits because the foreground operating cost was still high, despite the net environmental benefits from the product-substitution credits.
